content: 1. Lopinavir increases the levels of ponatinib by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily. 2. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Both lopinavir and primaquine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated. 9. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is structurally identical to lovastatin, and this interaction may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 10. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4 and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Resmetirom is an OATP1B1/3 substrate, and coadministration with inhibitors of these transporters should be avoided. 12. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both ribociclib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. 13. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Conversely, lopinavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4 and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4 and other mechanisms. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose of riociguat as needed. 17. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Lopinavir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Limit the rosuvastatin dose to 10 mg/day. The ritonavir component of lopinavir/ritonavir decreases rosuvastatin metabolism. 19. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg twice daily for patients with a platelet count of ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 20. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Both sertraline and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Both sevoflurane and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both siponimod and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. 25. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both solifenacin and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. 27. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Lopinavir and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 30. St. John's Wort decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both sunitinib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. 33. Lopinavir increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both tacrolimus and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. 35. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased tadalafil levels may lead to severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 36. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Lopinavir increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug due to the potential for increased toxicity. 38. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of tazemetostat with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 39. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Both tetrabenazine and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Tipranavir decreases the levels of lopinavir through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Conversely, lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated. 43. Lopinavir increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily. 44. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated. 46. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of topotecan by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. 47. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day prior to the next infusion. 48. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 49. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 51. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate according to product labeling. 52. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated. 53. Lopinavir increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 54. Lopinavir and vandetanib may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 55. Both vemurafenib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases the levels of vemurafenib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. 56. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 57. Lopinavir increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 58. Lopinavir increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%; reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 59. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 60. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 62. Lopinavir increases the levels of vorapaxar by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 63. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated. 64. Both vorinostat and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 65. Lopinavir increases the levels of vortioxetine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP2D6. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the vortioxetine dose by 50% when coadministered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 66. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 67. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. 68. Lopinavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. New-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. 69. Lopinavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 70. Both alfuzosin and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 71. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 72. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 73. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. Dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 74. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 75. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4.
